research_topic: Is lDDT-PLI, as aggregated by PLINDER's plinder.eval, a safe single objective for an automated research agent to optimize? And what minimal aggregation change makes it non-gameable, on NVIDIA GB200 aarch64 hardware.

research_hypothesis.open_problems: PLINDER's evaluation resource is becoming the default target for automated protein-ligand cofolding research, and lDDT-PLI is the headline number an optimizing agent will chase. Two properties of the reference implementation make that number unsafe as a sole objective. First, aggregation is coverage-blind: plinder.eval's get_average_ligand_scores averages only over reference ligands to which a model ligand was successfully assigned, and skips unassigned ones rather than scoring them zero. A predictor that emits a pose for only the easiest ligands is therefore rewarded, and the fewer poses it emits the higher its mean climbs. Second, aggregation is validity-blind: lDDT-PLI counts recovered protein-ligand contacts within a distance threshold and saturates once a ligand's heavy atoms sit anywhere in the correct pocket, so a compact blob collapsed onto the pocket centroid recovers most contacts while being chemically nonsense. The MLSB 2024 PLINDER challenge showed this concretely -- a degenerate 'Blackhole PLI Busted' entry reached median lDDT-PLI 0.67 at BiSyRMSD 7.93 A, far above the single real submission at 0.17. Both failure modes are properties of the aggregation step, not of the per-contact score, so both are fixable without touching OpenStructure's scorer. No published work quantifies how often they invert predictor rankings, and no published work verifies that the OpenStructure-based scores are numerically reproducible on aarch64, which is now the architecture of NVIDIA's Grace-Blackwell systems.
research_hypothesis.method: We propose CG-PLI (Coverage-Gated, validity-gated PLI), a minimal modification to the aggregation step of plinder.eval that leaves the per-ligand OpenStructure LDDTPLIScorer untouched. The reference aggregation over a system with reference ligands R and per-ligand scores s_i (None when unassigned) is mean over the assigned subset: PLI_ave = mean({s_i : s_i is not None}). CG-PLI makes two one-line changes. (1) Coverage gating: unassigned reference ligands contribute 0 rather than being dropped, so the denominator is |R| rather than the number of assignments. This makes the aggregate a lower bound on achievable quality and removes the incentive to abstain. (2) Validity gating: each per-ligand score is multiplied by a binary PoseBusters validity indicator v_i in {0,1}, so chemically implausible poses contribute nothing regardless of contact recovery. The resulting statistic is CG-PLI = (1/|R|) * sum_i v_i * s_i, with s_i := 0 for unassigned i. The theoretical motivation is that lDDT-PLI is a recall-style quantity computed on a self-selected support, and any recall-style score evaluated only where the predictor chose to answer is maximised by answering less. Coverage gating converts it from a conditional mean into an unconditional one, which is the standard fix for selective prediction. Validity gating adds the orthogonal physical-plausibility axis that PoseBusters established is necessary, at the level of the individual ligand rather than as a separately reported aggregate, so the two cannot be traded off against each other by reporting a high mean on a small valid subset. Both changes are monotone: CG-PLI <= PLI_ave always, with equality exactly when coverage is complete and every pose is PB-valid.
research_hypothesis.experimental_setup: Dataset: the PLINDER 2024-06/v2 MLSB subset, splits/mlsb/inputs.parquet, which is 346 single-ligand systems all belonging to the PLINDER test split, fetched anonymously over HTTPS from gs://plinder together with the corresponding systems/ shards that carry receptor.cif and ligand_files/*.sdf. Predictors: rather than porting three cofolding baselines to aarch64, which is out of scope, we construct a controlled family of predictors whose true geometric quality is known by construction, which is what is needed to test whether a metric ranks correctly. The family spans (a) reference, the holo ligand itself, quality rank 1; (b) perturbed-k, the holo ligand rigid-body displaced by a controlled RMSD of k in {0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8} A, monotonically decreasing quality; (c) blackhole, all ligand heavy atoms collapsed to the pocket centroid, chemically invalid by construction; (d) blackhole-busted, the same collapse followed by a minimal RDKit relaxation that restores bond lengths so it passes some PoseBusters checks, the MLSB degenerate entry; (e) decoy, an RDKit-generated conformer of the correct SMILES placed at the pocket centroid with random orientation; (f) abstain-p, the reference pose emitted for only the easiest fraction p in {0.25, 0.5} of systems ranked by pocket size and no pose otherwise, which probes coverage gaming specifically. Scoring: OpenStructure 2.9-2.11 installed from bioconda linux-aarch64 via micromamba, driving plinder.eval's LDDTPLIScorer and SCRMSDScorer with the PLINDER defaults substructure_match=True, add_mdl_contacts=True, resnum_alignments=False; PoseBusters, which is pure python and architecture-neutral, supplies v_i. Comparison: for each predictor we compute both the base aggregate PLI_ave and the proposed CG-PLI, plus BiSyRMSD and coverage for reporting. The ground-truth quality ordering over the predictor family is fixed a priori by construction (reference > perturbed-0.5 > perturbed-1 > perturbed-2 > perturbed-4 > perturbed-8 > decoy > blackhole-busted > blackhole, with abstain-p tied to reference on quality but penalised on coverage). We then measure the Spearman rank correlation between each metric's induced ordering and that a priori ordering. Reproducibility: the identical harness is run on GB200 aarch64 and on x86_64 managed compute, and we report the maximum absolute per-system difference in lDDT-PLI between architectures.
research_hypothesis.expected_result: We predict that the base aggregation fails to rank the predictor family correctly and the modification repairs it. Concretely, for PLI_ave we expect a Spearman rank correlation against the a priori quality ordering of roughly 0.3 to 0.6, driven by two specific inversions: blackhole-busted scoring near 0.6-0.7 and therefore placing above perturbed-4 and perturbed-8 despite BiSyRMSD near 8 A, reproducing the MLSB leaderboard observation at n=346 rather than at n=1; and abstain-0.25 scoring essentially equal to reference, near 0.95, despite answering on a quarter of the systems. For CG-PLI we expect a Spearman correlation above 0.95, with blackhole and blackhole-busted collapsing to below 0.05 because validity gating zeroes them, and abstain-0.25 falling to approximately 0.25 times its uncoverage-gated value, near 0.24, which restores its correct position. The primary-metric gap we therefore predict is a Spearman improvement of at least +0.4 absolute, from about 0.5 to above 0.95. Secondary predictions: coverage is 1.0 for all predictors except abstain-p where it is p by construction; BiSyRMSD tracks the a priori ordering well for the perturbed family, confirming it is the metric that lDDT-PLI most needs as a companion; and cross-architecture agreement between GB200 aarch64 and x86_64 shows a maximum absolute per-system lDDT-PLI difference below 1e-6, which would establish that OpenStructure-based PLINDER scoring is architecture-portable, a fact currently unverified in the literature and a prerequisite for running this benchmark on Grace-Blackwell hardware at all.
research_hypothesis.expected_conclusion: The practical value is that a two-line change to an aggregation function decides whether an autonomous research agent pointed at PLINDER optimises structure quality or learns to abstain and to emit chemically invalid blobs. Because lDDT-PLI is a recall-style score computed on a support the predictor itself selects, it is gameable in exactly the way selective-prediction metrics are always gameable, and the fix is the same one the selective-prediction literature already uses: score the whole reference set, not the answered subset. Adding per-ligand validity gating closes the second, orthogonal loophole that PoseBusters identified but that the community currently reports as a separate column, where it can be traded off rather than enforced. Neither change requires retraining any model, modifying OpenStructure, or altering the PLINDER dataset, so CG-PLI can be adopted as a drop-in reporting standard. The accompanying cross-architecture check matters for a different reason: it is what makes the whole benchmark usable on NVIDIA Grace-Blackwell aarch64 systems, where the pip-installable half of this software stack does not exist and the evaluation half has never been validated.

experimental_design.experiment_summary: The system under test is a scoring pipeline, not a predictive model: it ingests a protein-ligand complex plus a candidate ligand pose and emits a scalar quality judgement. The experiment asks whether the aggregation rule that PLINDER's plinder.eval uses to turn per-ligand lDDT-PLI into a per-method headline number preserves the true quality ordering of the methods it is asked to rank. Workflow: (1) fetch the PLINDER 2024-06/v2 MLSB manifest (splits/mlsb/inputs.parquet, 346 single-ligand test systems) and the corresponding systems/ shards anonymously over HTTPS from gs://plinder, taking receptor.cif and ligand_files/*.sdf per system; (2) synthesise a controlled predictor family whose true geometric quality is fixed by construction rather than learned -- reference (the holo ligand), perturbed-k for k in {0.5,1,2,4,8} A of rigid-body displacement, decoy (an RDKit conformer of the correct SMILES dropped at the pocket centroid with random orientation), blackhole (all heavy atoms collapsed onto the pocket centroid), blackhole-busted (that collapse followed by minimal RDKit relaxation restoring bond lengths), and abstain-p for p in {0.25,0.5} (the reference pose emitted on only the easiest fraction p of systems, nothing elsewhere); (3) score every (system, predictor) pair on three independent axes -- lDDT-PLI contact recovery, symmetry-corrected BiSyRMSD, and PoseBusters chemical validity; (4) aggregate each predictor's per-system scores under the incumbent rule PLI_ave and under the proposed CG-PLI, and measure how faithfully each aggregation reproduces the a priori quality ordering. Scale is fitted to the runner by choosing a subset that is 346 systems rather than the full 1,036-system test split, which keeps the systems/ download at 38 GB against 939 GB of Lustre scratch and keeps wall time in minutes: scoring is O(atoms) per system and embarrassingly parallel over 32 cores, with the GPU carrying the batched rigid-body transforms and pairwise distance matrices that generate and score the perturbed family. sanity mode runs 2 synthetic systems with no network access and asserts the algebraic invariants; pilot mode runs 20 real systems; full mode runs all 346.

evaluation_metrics.name: spearman_correlation
evaluation_metrics.description: Correctness criteria: an aggregation rule is correct to the extent that the ordering it induces over the predictor family matches the ordering fixed a priori by construction, namely reference > perturbed-0.5 > perturbed-1 > perturbed-2 > perturbed-4 > perturbed-8 > decoy > blackhole-busted > blackhole, with abstain-p slotted by its coverage-discounted expected quality p. Because that ordering is known by construction rather than estimated, there is no label noise and disagreement is attributable entirely to the metric. Calculation method: for each aggregation rule A, form the vector a = (A(pred_1), ..., A(pred_m)) over the m predictors and the vector t = (m, m-1, ..., 1) of a priori quality ranks, then report rho = spearmanr(t, a).statistic, the Pearson correlation of the rank-transformed vectors. Confidence intervals come from bootstrapping over the 346 systems: resample systems with replacement 1,000 times, recompute every predictor's aggregate on the resample, and report the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of rho. Task appropriateness: the quantity at stake is ordinal, since a benchmark's job is to rank methods, and rho is invariant to any monotone rescaling of the metric, so it isolates ranking fidelity from calibration. Relevant visualizations: a slope chart pairing each predictor's PLI_ave rank with its CG-PLI rank so that inversions appear as crossing lines, and a bar chart of rho per aggregation rule with bootstrap error bars.

evaluation_metrics.name: lddt_pli
evaluation_metrics.description: Correctness criteria: the fraction of reference protein-ligand heavy-atom contacts, defined as pairs within 6.0 A in the reference complex, whose interatomic distance is preserved in the model pose within any of the tolerance thresholds 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 A, averaged over thresholds. A ligand atom must first be assigned to a reference ligand atom by graph isomorphism with symmetry correction. Calculation method: score_i = mean over the four thresholds of |{(p,l) in C_ref : | d_model(p,l) - d_ref(p,l) | < tau}| / |C_ref|, per reference ligand i; unassignable ligands yield None. Aggregation is where the two rules differ: PLI_ave = mean over the assigned subset only, whereas CG-PLI = (1/|R|) * sum_i v_i * s_i over all reference ligands with s_i := 0 when unassigned and v_i the PoseBusters indicator. Task appropriateness: lDDT-PLI is superposition-free, so it does not require a global alignment that a badly placed ligand would corrupt, which is why PLINDER adopted it; the same insensitivity is what lets a pocket-centroid blob score well, which is the failure this experiment measures. Relevant visualizations: violin plots of the per-system distribution per predictor, and a scatter of lDDT-PLI against BiSyRMSD with the degenerate predictors highlighted to expose the region of high score at high RMSD.

evaluation_metrics.name: bisy_rmsd
evaluation_metrics.description: Correctness criteria: the binding-site-superposed, symmetry-corrected root-mean-square deviation in Angstroms between model and reference ligand heavy atoms, lower being better, with the conventional success threshold at 2 A. Calculation method: superpose the model receptor onto the reference receptor using binding-site residues only, apply that transform to the model ligand, then minimise RMSD over all graph automorphisms of the ligand to remove symmetry artefacts. Task appropriateness: BiSyRMSD is a placement metric rather than a contact-recovery metric, so it is sensitive exactly where lDDT-PLI saturates, and it is the companion axis PLINDER already reports; including it lets the experiment show that the degenerate predictors are unambiguously bad on an independent axis at the same time as they look good on lDDT-PLI. Relevant visualizations: cumulative distribution of per-system RMSD per predictor with the 2 A threshold marked.

evaluation_metrics.name: pb_valid
evaluation_metrics.description: Correctness criteria: the fraction of emitted poses passing the full PoseBusters check suite, covering ligand internal geometry (bond lengths, bond angles, aromatic ring planarity, internal steric clash, stereochemistry, energy ratio against an ensemble of generated conformers) and intermolecular geometry (no protein-ligand steric clash, ligand inside the declared pocket volume). Calculation method: run posebusters in redock mode against the reference ligand and receptor and take the conjunction of all checks as the binary indicator v_i, then report the mean of v_i over emitted poses. Task appropriateness: PoseBusters is pure python and therefore architecture-neutral, which makes it the one axis guaranteed to be comparable between aarch64 and x86_64; it also supplies exactly the binary gate the proposed method needs. Relevant visualizations: a stacked bar of per-check pass rates per predictor, which shows which specific check the blackhole-busted predictor was engineered to defeat.

evaluation_metrics.name: coverage
evaluation_metrics.description: Correctness criteria: the fraction of reference ligands across the evaluated systems for which the predictor emitted a pose that could be assigned to that reference ligand. Calculation method: coverage = (number of assigned reference ligands) / (total number of reference ligands), computed over the whole evaluation set rather than per system. Task appropriateness: coverage is the quantity the incumbent aggregation silently conditions on, so reporting it is what makes PLI_ave interpretable at all; the abstain-p predictors exist specifically to make the dependence measurable, and their construction guarantees coverage equals p. Relevant visualizations: a two-dimensional plot of PLI_ave against coverage with iso-CG-PLI contours overlaid, which shows geometrically that the incumbent rule lets a predictor trade coverage for score at constant apparent quality.

evaluation_metrics.name: cross_arch_max_abs_diff
evaluation_metrics.description: Correctness criteria: the largest absolute difference in per-system lDDT-PLI between the aarch64 GB200 run and the x86_64 run of the identical harness on the identical inputs; agreement below 1e-6 is treated as bitwise-equivalent for reporting purposes and anything above 1e-3 would invalidate cross-architecture comparison of published PLINDER numbers. Calculation method: max over systems and predictors of |score_aarch64 - score_x86|, with the count and identity of systems exceeding 1e-6 reported alongside. Task appropriateness: no published work establishes that the PLINDER evaluation stack is numerically portable to aarch64, and the entire premise of running this benchmark on NVIDIA Grace-Blackwell hardware depends on it; the check costs one extra run and converts an unstated assumption into a measured fact. Relevant visualizations: a histogram of per-system absolute differences on a log axis.

datasets_to_use: PLINDER 2024-06/v2 MLSB subset (splits/mlsb/inputs.parquet, 346 single-ligand systems from the PLINDER test split)

proposed_method.description: An aggregation rule for per-ligand lDDT-PLI that replaces plinder.eval's conditional mean over assigned ligands with an unconditional mean over all reference ligands, and multiplies each per-ligand score by a binary PoseBusters validity indicator. CG-PLI = (1/|R|) * sum_i v_i * s_i, with s_i := 0 for unassigned reference ligands. The per-ligand scorer is untouched, so the change is confined to two lines of the aggregation function and is a drop-in replacement for any existing PLINDER-based report. Novelty is in recognising lDDT-PLI as a recall-style score computed on a predictor-selected support, which makes abstention profitable, and in moving physical validity from a separately reported and therefore tradeable column into a per-ligand gate.

comparative_methods.description: The incumbent rule as implemented in plinder.eval's get_average_ligand_scores: average per-ligand lDDT-PLI over only those reference ligands that received an assignable model pose, skipping unassigned ligands rather than scoring them zero, and reporting PoseBusters validity separately rather than gating on it. This is the number currently reported on PLINDER-derived leaderboards and therefore the objective an automated agent would optimise.

The second aggregation plinder.eval already emits, weighting each per-ligand lDDT-PLI by the ligand's heavy-atom count before averaging over the assigned subset. It is included to establish that the failure is caused by conditioning on the assigned subset rather than by the unweighted mean specifically, since PLI_wave shares the coverage blindness and the validity blindness while differing in weighting.
